recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you break the numerator up and which two standard limits you use.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Split into two standard limits
steps.margin_note: First mark. Group the numerator as (eˣ − 1) and (sin x), not as eˣ and (sin x + 1). The −1 belongs with eˣ, because eˣ − 1 is the standard form.
steps.memory_tip: The lone −1 in the numerator is there to pair with eˣ. Keep them together and both pieces become standard limits.
lines: Putting x = 0 gives 0/0, so the numerator is regrouped first.
∴ lim(x → 0) (eˣ − sin x − 1)/x = lim(x → 0) (eˣ − 1)/x − lim(x → 0) (sin x)/x
Both of these limits exist, so the difference may be taken term by term.

recall.must_convey: That the numerator is regrouped as (eˣ − 1) − sin x, giving (eˣ − 1)/x minus sin x/x.
accept: keep e to the x minus one together and sin x separate
split it into e power x minus one by x and sin x by x
regroup the numerator so the minus one goes with e to the x
e power x minus one ni kalipi rasi, sin x ni veru chesi rayali
two standard limits, e power x minus one over x and sin x over x

steps.why: Direct substitution gives 0/0. Splitting a limit into a difference is only allowed when each piece has a limit of its own, and both pieces here are the standard limits the chapter is built on, so the split is safe and each piece is already known.
common_mistakes: Grouping as eˣ − (sin x + 1), which leaves neither piece in standard form.
Splitting the fraction but writing the second piece as sin x, not sin x/x.

steps.label: Apply both limits and subtract
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both standard limits equal 1, so the answer is 1 − 1 = 0. Write the two limits out before subtracting — the mark is for using them, not for the zero alone.
steps.memory_tip: Both standard limits here are worth exactly 1, so the answer is the difference of two ones.
lines: We know lim(x → 0) (eˣ − 1)/x = 1  and  lim(x → 0) (sin x)/x = 1

recall.must_convey: That both standard limits equal 1, so the value is 1 − 1 = 0.
accept: both limits are one so one minus one is zero
e power x minus one by x is one and sin x by x is one
rendu limits one, kaabatti answer zero

steps.why: Quoting both standard limits is what earns this mark. A bare 0 with no working could have come from substituting x = 0 into the numerator, which is not a valid method.
common_mistakes: Writing 1 + 1 = 2 by missing the minus sign in front of sin x.
Giving the answer as 0 with no working, so the method mark is lost.

insider_note: Regroup as (eˣ − 1) − sin x so each piece over x is a standard limit. Both come to 1, so they cancel and the answer is 0.
